text:
maya: quick question — for the console + internal platform APIs, are we leaning proto-first gRPC or sticking with REST/JSON at the gateway? trying to scope routing/quota work
alex: proto-first makes life nicer for typed clients and reduces marshalling errors. also smaller payloads. but it complicates browser clients unless we add grpc-web or translate at edge
nton y: +1 on typed contracts. main concern is cross-team adoption and debugging. JSON is easy to inspect in logs/mitm and easy for quick curl checks
sara: for telemetry and tracing we need consistent headers and path shape. grpc streams and unary look different in traces; our traces expect http.path and http.status now
kevin: if we do proto-first we should standardize transcoding rules at the gateway. automatic transcoding -> json for public routes, keep grpc internally. avoids having two separate contracts
maya: current thinking: internal service-to-service gRPC with protos, but expose REST for third-party and console via gateway that does stable JSON shaping. but we need a clear shim strategy for routing policies + quotas
alex: what about a lightweight compatibility layer: gateway does proto->json mapping but also emits canonical operation names for quotas/routing so our console metrics don't need to handle dual shapes
sara: agreed. quota keys need to be stable across transports. suggest canonical op name header: X-Redwood-Op: <svc>.<method>
kevin: +1. also include X-Redwood-Shard for routing policy hints (region/tier). keeps routing logic simple at edge
nton y: curious about developer UX. if proto changes, how do we version? use method-level versioning in proto package or use gateway to map v2 routes to old method names?
maya: prefer proto versioning (package/service v2). gateway config can map /v2/* to new proto package. keeps services clean and reduces gateway magic
alex: ops question: how does this affect our dashboards? telemetry currently aggregates by http.path. we'll need to emit metrics by op name and include transport tag (grpc/json) so we can compare 
sara: add telemetry migration plan: 1) emit op_name tag alongside path 2) make dashboards query op_name by default 3) fallback to path
kevin: and for quota enforcement: central quota service should consume op_name header and ignore body shape. that centralization avoids duplication across gateway/proxy implementations
nton y: what about browser clients? grpc-web + envoy vs JSON. grpc-web requires extra work but gives us parity. is it worth it for the console?
maya: console traffic is small but latency-sensitive for streaming logs and events. that might benefit from grpc-web streaming. but we can start with unary JSON for console UX v1 and iterate
alex: practical ask: can someone prototype a gateway rule that: 1) accepts JSON POST /v1/* 2) transcodes to proto and forwards to internal svc 3) injects X-Redwood-Op header and X-Redwood-Shard
sara: I can do a stubbed env config for envoy lua filter to set headers based on route metadata. share proto-to-route mapping in repo
kevin: i'll sketch quota service changes (ignore content-type and use op header). will add acceptance tests for mismatched shapes
nton y: should we document this in the API standards doc? -> add section "transport-agnostic op names and gateway transcoding"
maya: yes. action items: maya to run 2-week spike for gateway transcoding + telemetry tags; sara to prototype envoy header injector; kevin to update quota service test plan; alex to update dashboards with op_name tag
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled ephemeral staging cluster for spike at 1876550200 (ETA ~10m) :rocket:
maya: thanks — will post progress here. if spike goes well we propose proto-first internal + gateway-transcoding policy for October rollout :thumbsup:
